leads.summary: Transparent theme bar backgrounds bypass the pill wallpaper contrast path
leads.consequence: For [bar] background/background-alpha=0, a light wallpaper, pills=section, transparent=false and no pill-text override, the new pillForeground assumes an opaque dark bar when selecting white text although a 10%-white pill actually overlays light wallpaper. Sandbox model run: assumed backdrop #282828, actual #f6f6f6, chosen white contrast 1.08:1 versus dark alternative 17.61:1. Any partially transparent bar background can similarly shift the actual contrast. Respect the drawn bar's alpha and wallpaper, or use the sampler for translucent bar backgrounds, not only requestedTransparent.

leads.summary: Open #13570 independently owns the same group key and bar slot geometry
leads.consequence: #13570 makes group mandatory oval grouping whenever layout entries carry group, whereas this PR uses that same key to split pills. A three-way file merge with #13570 using its actual Bar.qml parent (current base tip) produces 13 conflict blocks, including center lists, ModuleSlot and paint. Both heads are diverged and #13570 is MERGEABLE against base separately. If maintainers resolve those conflicts by retaining both paints, the documented group example draws an oval underneath every corresponding pill, so choose compatible precedence and geometry explicitly before both land; this visual result is a conditional prediction, not a completed merge/test.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator git merge-file in coordinator/h5, Opus cross-check from public sources

leads.summary: Combine #13138's floating-bar sampler inputs with --blend when stacking the bar PRs
leads.consequence: #13138 introduces --inset and a shifted crop for floating bars and changes the caller; this PR introduces --blend in the same argument parser and replaces the same sampler caller. Using their common file base in a read-only git merge-file yields 2 conflicts in the sampler and 3 in Bar.qml. Both PRs are diverged, though #13138 is MERGEABLE against base. Merging them requires preserving both sets of flags and cropping/blending; accepting either side alone makes floating translucent pill text sample the wrong strip or discards the blend. This is an integration blocker, not a failure of this PR by itself.

leads.summary: The end-user bar manual omits pills from its bar appearance and config guide
leads.consequence: The manual teaches position, transparency, and the complete sample shell.json bar subtree but never introduces the new pills key or links to its new docs. A reader customizing the bar from the manual has no way to discover the option there. Add pills and link docs/omarchy-shell.md#bar-pills next to transparency, with the explicit caveat that the current omarchy bar CLI has no pills subcommand (bin/omarchy-bar:12-48,207-218).

leads.summary: The new zero-padding/gap test inspects call-site text but never exercises the zero token reader
leads.consequence: A plausible regression that makes barInsetToken(key,fallback) return fallback even when the override is 0 still passes the new zero-padding/gap regex at bar-test.sh:443, because that assertion only matches the two property declarations and the VM test drives barToken, not barInsetToken. Then a user setting pill-gap=0 gets a 6px gap and pill-padding=0 gets 4px. Assert both values through applyShellValues and barInsetToken (including nonzero cases) in the existing VM fixture. Source-level test-fidelity finding, not a claim that the current reader is broken.

retro:
# RETRO: #13139 follow-up round 2

## Worked well

- Running the Opus review and the Sol hunt in parallel, then triaging the hunter's leads, worked. H5 (#13570 owning the same `group` key) was a cross-PR issue that Opus did not look for, and it checked out.
- The neutral H1 follow-up let Opus show the lead was pre-existing behaviour, not a regression. That kept a misleading finding out of the comment.
- The Opus self-check caught real lost qualifiers:
  - "on a drawn bar";
  - the transparent branch and "not tested" in the suggestion;
  - the wrong source credited for the ghost offset;
  - the stale "current base".

## Avoidable friction

- Two editorial rounds were spent on length. Check 2 ran on a draft at 1,512 visible characters because the length was not re-measured after the editorial fix. Always re-measure before `check-comment`.
- Pasting the reproducers verbatim keeps their H1 headings inside the collapsed blocks. That is fine, but a reproducer file without a top-level `#` heading would render more neatly.

## Process notes

- Between intake and completion, the base moved twice (324f0ba, then 8b4eae6). Base drift on long-running follow-ups should be checked again at completion, as was done here.
- The Opus agent wrote `final.md` itself, and `save-handback` also saved `final-report.md`. The two differ only in formatting; both are kept.
- No process deviations.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** All seven earlier findings are resolved at `e3d713c`; one minor new issue: the drag ghost can hide the dragged widget on a contrasting pill.

Follows the [second review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13139#issuecomment-5852581369) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13139#issuecomment-5866111592).

### Drag ghost hides the widget on a contrasting pill

With pills on, widgets use the pill text colour, but on a drawn bar the drag ghost is filled with the bar background. With `[bar] pill = "{{ foreground }}"` both are the same colour (contrast 1.00): the ghost is an empty box. **Impact:** drag feedback only; stock themes with just `"pills": "section"` are fine.

**Suggested change:** on a drawn bar, fill the ghost with the pill as drawn: `root.pillsOn ? Qt.tint(root.background, root.pillFill) : root.background` (not tested).

<details><summary>Reproducer (computation at e3d713c, not rendered)</summary>

# N1: with a contrasting pill colour, the drag ghost draws the widget in its own fill colour

Kind: computation from source with the PR's own colour helpers (`shell/plugins/bar/BarModel.js` at `e3d713c6`). Not a rendering; not observed on screen.

Source facts used:
- `Bar.qml` `pillForeground` (lines 96-101): with `[bar] pill` set and `[bar] pill-text` unset, widget text is `BarModel.pickTextColor(bar text, theme background, pill blended over the bar background)`. On a drawn bar `pillTextSampled` is false, so `barForeground` is this pill text (lines 102-104), and `WidgetButton` and the tray's bar icons draw in it.
- `Bar.qml` `DragGhostPanel` (lines 1478-1500): the ghost is `grabToImage` of the widget drawn over a `BorderSurface` whose `color` is `root.background` (`Color.bar.background`) on a drawn bar, at opacity 0.94, with a 1 px border in `root.barForeground`.

Run from the root of an omarchy checkout at `e3d713c6`:

```js
// ghost-contrast.js
const path = require('path')
const bar = require(path.resolve(process.argv[2] || '.', 'shell/plugins/bar/BarModel.js'))

const themes = [
  // [name, colors.toml foreground, colors.toml background]
  ['Tokyo Night', '#a9b1d6', '#1a1b26'],
  ['Catppuccin Latte', '#4c4f69', '#eff1f5']
]
for (const [name, fg, bg] of themes) {
  // [bar] pill = "{{ foreground }}" on a drawn bar: pillRaised is false, so the
  // backdrop is the pill at alpha 1.
  const pill = bar.blendHex(fg, 1, bg)
  // pillForeground with [bar] pill-text unset.
  const pillText = bar.pickTextColor(fg, bg, pill)
  console.log(`${name}, [bar] pill = "{{ foreground }}"`)
  console.log(`  pill ${pill}, widget text ${pillText}, contrast on the pill ${bar.contrastRatio(pillText, pill).toFixed(2)}`)
  console.log(`  drag ghost fill ${bg}, contrast of the dragged widget on it ${bar.contrastRatio(pillText, bg).toFixed(2)}`)
}
```

`node ghost-contrast.js` (Node v26.7.0), actual output:

```text
Tokyo Night, [bar] pill = "{{ foreground }}"
  pill #a9b1d6, widget text #1a1b26, contrast on the pill 8.10
  drag ghost fill #1a1b26, contrast of the dragged widget on it 1.00
Catppuccin Latte, [bar] pill = "{{ foreground }}"
  pill #4c4f69, widget text #eff1f5, contrast on the pill 7.06
  drag ghost fill #eff1f5, contrast of the dragged widget on it 1.00
```

The picked text is right for the pill (8.10 and 7.06), but the ghost fill is the bar background, which here equals the picked text, so the dragged widget's glyph and the ghost's 1 px border have the same colour as the ghost fill. With the stock template and only `"pills": "section"` (the raised default pill), the pill text stays the theme text and the ghost reads as before (8.1 on Tokyo Night, 7.06 on Catppuccin Latte).
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Earlier findings:** the `"pill": false` colour is resolved as scoped (documented, not changed). The pills-off anchor shift, section-end overhang, docs reference and layer-rules link stay fixed after the amend. The drag z-order and the tray popup colour are fixed in this revision. The drag ghost issue above was not raised before; its code is unchanged since the first revision.

**Verified:**
- `bar-test.sh` (148 checks) and `bar-text-color-test.sh` (8 checks) pass at `e3d713c`, and also with the PR diff applied to `324f0ba`, the base at review time.
- Neighbouring pills are exactly `pill-gap` apart for odd gaps. In the same model check, the previous revision put them one pixel further apart.
- `[bar] pill-gap = 0` and `pill-padding = 0` read as 0, through the real `Style.qml` token functions.
- The drag z-order matches Qt's paint order, the ghost offset matches the slot layout in `Bar.qml`, and the sampler re-run matches Quickshell v0.3.1's `Process`. None was observed on screen.
- `bar.pillsOn` reaches the plugin facade, so a cloned tray's bar icons follow the pill text colour.

**Related PR #13570:** it uses the layout `"group"` key to draw ovals, while this PR uses it to split pill runs. With this PR's `Bar.qml` and `BarModel.js` rebased onto #13570's base, a three-way merge with #13570's head leaves 13 conflict blocks in `Bar.qml` and 1 in `BarModel.js`. These include `ModuleSlot` and the anchored-centre lists.

**Optional test improvement:** most new round-2 checks match source text. A mutant that draws each horizontal pill from the wrong gap half (1 px off for odd gaps) still passes all 148 checks. Adding `barInsetToken` to the functions the existing `vm` harness extracts from `Style.qml` would make the zero-token check behavioural.

# T1 (test validity): the round-2 geometry checks pin source text, not geometry

Kind: mutation run of the PR's own `test/shell.d/bar-test.sh` at `e3d713c6`, in an isolated sandbox (Node v26.7.0). Not a product defect; a note on what the new tests can and cannot catch.

## Mutant 1: pill drawn from the wrong gap half

One-line change in `shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml` (the pill `Rectangle` inside `ModuleSlot`):

```diff
-      x: root.vertical ? inset : slot.pillGapLead
+      x: root.vertical ? inset : slot.pillGapTrail
```

With an odd `pill-gap` this moves every horizontal pill 1 px towards its end, so the outer pill no longer sits `pill-inset` from the bar start and the padding inside the pill becomes uneven.

`bash test/shell.d/bar-test.sh` on the mutated tree, actual result: exit 0, 148 of 148 `ok` lines, including:

```text
ok - the gap halves of two neighbouring pills add up to pill-gap
ok - a pill is drawn between the two gap halves of its run
ok - pill-padding and pill-gap keep a deliberate 0
ok - dragging the first widget of a pill keeps the pill under its neighbours
ok - the drag ghost stays under the pointer inside a pill
```

The regex for "a pill is drawn between the two gap halves of its run" checks the `width` line, not `x`.

## Mutant 2: the old symmetric split

```diff
 function pillGapLead(pillGap) {
-  return Math.floor(pillGap / 2)
+  return Math.round(pillGap / 2)
 }
```

Actual result: exit 1. The identity check passes, and the behavioural `sectionEndMargin` case catches it:

```text
ok - the gap halves of two neighbouring pills add up to pill-gap
ok - an even gap splits evenly
expected: -1
actual:   -2
not ok - the start of a section takes the smaller half of an odd gap
```

`bar.pillGapLead(7) + (7 - bar.pillGapLead(7)) === 7` holds for any return value, so that assertion cannot fail; the odd-gap split is covered by the `sectionEndMargin` cases instead.

A behavioural alternative already fits the file's style: the test runs `Style.qml`'s real `barToken` through `vm`, and the same harness can call `barInsetToken('pill-gap', 6)` with `[bar] pill-gap = 0` (0 at `e3d713c6`, 6 with the previous `barToken` reader).
</details>
